Choose a pattern, inspect its slide, and copy the Markdown below it. These
examples use the supplied Nocturne theme. Choose light or dark mode, or switch
to the presenter view to see its notes. No stylesheet edits are needed.

## Use a pattern in your talk

1. Download the [complete Markdown](_generated/source/patterns.qmd.txt).
2. Save the [diagram](_generated/source/two-views.svg) and
   [texture](_generated/source/texture.svg) in your deck's `assets/` folder.
3. Copy the selected slide into your talk and replace its words and picture path.
4. Keep a useful description inside `![description]`. Use `.decorative` only
   when an image adds no information.

Picture credits link to `#sources`. When copying one slide, either copy and adapt
the source-record appendix too, or replace the sample link with your own source
URL. If you copy the appendix, update its return links to IDs in your talk.

The examples use these deck settings. If your file already has YAML front matter,
merge them into its existing `deck` section. For a new file, put the complete
block at the start, before the first slide. `counter: presenter` keeps slide numbers in the presenter
view and hides them from the audience. Open the full deck from the preview
header to see the counter policy; the embedded lab hides deck navigation controls.

```yaml
---
pagetitle: My talk
deck:
  theme: nocturne
  color-mode: auto
  counter: presenter
  text-fit: true
  overflow: fit-scroll
---
```

Try the [statement](?slide=1), [quotation](?slide=2), and
[presenter-only counter](?slide=10) examples as well.

## Choose the picture layout

| Goal | Pattern | What to change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keep the whole image, with a caption | [Contained picture](?slide=3) | Replace the described `.ds-fit` image. |
| Cover the slide with a picture | [Full-slide picture](?slide=4) | Use `.ds-full` and `.ds-fill`; fill may crop edges. |
| Put text over a picture | [Picture and panel](?slide=5), [text without a panel](syntax-examples.qmd?slide=35) | Use `.ds-layer`; add `.ds-panel` for a solid panel. |
| Add a decorative background | [Background](?slide=6) | Set `data-background-image` on the heading. |
| Explain a picture in steps | [Picture left](?slide=7) | Keep the picture in `.ds-left`, the explanation in `.ds-right`. |
| Put the explanation first | [Picture right](?slide=8) | Swap the `.ds-left` and `.ds-right` roles. |
| Place several pictures | [Picture grid](?slide=9) | Put a `.ds-media` block for each image in `.ds-grid`. |

`.ds-fit` retains the whole image. `.ds-fill` covers its box and can crop it.
A normal image's description also becomes a caption. Full-slide images keep
the description for screen readers and hide that caption. Decorative backgrounds
have no accessible image description; put any essential meaning in the slide text.

Use `.credit` for a short attribution and link it to a longer source record in
the appendix. The theme reserves space for the credit, caption and section label.
For an important single claim, use `.statement`; for a quotation, use `.quote`
on the slide and `.source` on the attribution.

## More authoring patterns

The [interactive feature tour](example.qmd) covers synchronized code and equations,
matched colors, dimmed reveals, footnotes and appendix links.
[Semantic slides](semantic-authoring.md) gives the complete syntax for these roles.
[Layout and class reference](quarto-class-map.md) also covers cards, grids,
video/audio controls, filters, transitions and small interactions.

To put the same decorative image behind every slide, set `background-image`
under `deck` in front matter. Use `.no-background` on a slide that should omit it.
See the [background settings](build-a-deck-from-markdown.md)
for fit, opacity and filter options. Add these entries to your existing `deck`
section to use the supplied texture throughout the talk:

```yaml
deck:
  background-image: assets/texture.svg
```
